audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly told you to engage "on Powder Kegs's cooldown" and called the ability "Powder Kegs".
audit.why: Powder Keg has a cooldown of 0 in the kit — it is charge-based, so there is never a moment when it is "down". The real timing gate is whether a barrel is armed near you, which is why the keg-blast/Counter Strike interaction (E dodges his auto and Parrrley but only reduces the keg AoE) is the deciding one.
audit.corrected: Advice re-keyed to armed barrels instead of an imaginary cooldown, and the ability named Powder Keg.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's R was called "Grandmaster at Arms" in whys[4] and spikes[2].text, with no cooldown given.
audit.why: Grandmaster at Arms is Jax's title; the ultimate is Grandmaster's Might (110/100/90s), which the full layer already names correctly — the two layers disagreed.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster's Might used in both places and its 110s rank-1 cooldown stated at the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradicted the packet chart and the page's own why-strings: Level 1 Gangplank, Level 3 Jax, Levels 4-5 Jax, First item Jax.
audit.why: The packet chart is Skill/Skill/Skill/Gangplank/Gangplank/Gangplank/Jax, and whys[2] calls level 3 "a genuine wash", whys[3] says 4-5 "tilts his way" and whys[5] says the poke lane "stays his" through the first item. The mirror audit reached the same four flips.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3, 4-5 and first item flipped in both layers as one atomic group, ratings moved with them.

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Gangplank's Powder Kegs is down.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges his Parrrley, but he just holds range. Trade only with no keg armed beside you.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gangplank must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Counter Strike only eats the autos he refuses to throw — hold the wave near you and farm the standoff.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Powder Kegs's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window: a second keg charge lets him chain barrels and detonate them with Parrrley from range. Give nothing and stay healthy.

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Powder Kegs's cooldown.
edits.after: Trinity Force lands, but keg knockback and slow let him refuse — you must land Leap Strike first.

edits.before: Pop his barrels — E his combo, out-scale his crit. Jax wins by trading around Gangplank's Powder Kegs and cashing the pattern: deny barrels and out-scale his crit.
edits.after: Pop his barrels — E his combo, out-scale his crit. Jax wins by killing each keg before it arms and cashing the pattern: deny barrels and out-scale his crit.

edits.before: Deny barrels and out-scale his crit. Track Powder Kegs before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Deny barrels and out-scale his crit. Powder Keg is charge-based, not on cooldown — kill each one before it arms.

edits.before: Gangplank wins by landing Powder Kegs, denying your pattern, and kiting you off the wave.
edits.after: Gangplank wins by chaining Powder Kegs, popping them with Parrrley, and kiting you off the wave.

edits.before: - Jax vs Gangplank - Track: Gangplank Powder Kegs. - Keep the wave on your side. - Engage only on Powder Kegs's cooldown. - Don't chase past the wave. - Ultimate = kill windows only.
edits.after: - Jax vs Gangplank - Track: Gangplank's Powder Keg charges. - Keep the wave on your side. - Leap in only when no keg is armed. - Don't chase past the wave. - Ultimate = kill windows only.

edits.before: - Gangplank Powder Kegs: matchup-defining — Pop barrels to deny poke + gold. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gangplank Powder Keg: matchup-defining — no cooldown, only charges, so kill each barrel to deny the poke and the gold. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Powder Kegs: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If behind, farm safe and let your spikes re-open the lane.
edits.after: Trade strictly around his kegs: with no barrel armed, run your full pattern; with one armed, give nothing. If behind, farm safe and let your spikes re-open the lane.

edits.before: Track Gangplank's Powder Kegs: Pop barrels to deny poke + gold. When it is down — Q-E-W him.
edits.after: Track Gangplank's Powder Keg charges: kill barrels to deny poke + gold. With none armed — Q-E-W him.

edits.before: Track Gangplank's Powder Kegs before you commit
edits.after: Track Gangplank's armed Powder Keg before a commit

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms is purely defensive into him — he zones with Cannon Barrage and pokes from outside your leap, so your level-6 spike buys survival, not a kill.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might is purely defensive into him — he zones with Cannon Barrage and pokes from outside your leap, so your level-6 spike buys survival, not a kill.

edits.before: R (Grandmaster at Arms) hands you the Armor/MR steroid and a third-hit on-hit, but here it's defensive — he kites with keg slows and zones with Cannon Barrage from outside your leap, so your ult buys survival, not a kill.
edits.after: R (Grandmaster's Might, 110s at rank 1) hands you the Armor/MR steroid and the third-hit magic damage, but here it's defensive — he kites on keg slows and zones with Cannon Barrage from outside your leap, so it buys survival.

notes: Powder Keg has cd 0 in the kit — it is charge-based, so every "engage on Powder Kegs's cooldown" line on this page was advice keyed to a cooldown that does not exist. Re-keyed to armed barrels. Jax's ultimate is Grandmaster's Might; the content layer called it "Grandmaster at Arms" (his title) while the full layer had it right — the kit file carries no ability names, so this correction is from Riot naming, not the kit. Chart: four rows flipped to match the packet and the mirror.
